Alpha Brownsville- 2nd Grade
PTMC Jr. Final Project Report: Growing Radishes in Lunar Simulant
Team Name: Lunar Radish Growers
Background/Reasoning
Radishes were chosen due to their fast-growing nature, typically ready for harvest within 20–30
days, aligning with the 8-week grow period. Our experiment aimed to investigate the impact of
varying soil compositions and amendments on radish growth in lunar regolith simulant,
simulating lunar farming conditions.
Hypothesis
We hypothesized that radishes grown in a mixture of 50% lunar simulant and 50% earth soil
with additional compost and bone meal would exhibit the best growth in terms of sprout count,
plant height, and leaf development compared to other compositions.
Independent Variable
●
Soil composition: Varying percents of lunar simulant, earth soil, compost, and bone meal.
Dependent Variable
●
Plant growth, measured by:
○
Sprout count
○
Plant height
○
Leaf count and condition
○
Radish formation (presence and size)
Controls/Constants
●
Light: 12-hour day/night cycle using grow lights.
●
Water: 1 ounce every 3 days (increased after Week 7 to address wilting).
●
Temperature: room temperature.
●
Seeds: Same radish variety.

Procedures
1.
Setup:
○
Prepared six pots with the following compositions:
■
Pot 1 (Control): 100% earth soil
■
Pot 2: 75% lunar simulant, 15% earth soil, 10% earthworm casings, 1 cup
compost, 1 tablespoon bone meal
■
Pot 3: 75% lunar simulant, 15% earth soil, 10% earthworm casings (no
compost or bone meal)
■
Pot 4: 50% lunar simulant, 40% earth soil, 10% earthworm casings, 1 cup
compost, 1 tablespoon bone meal
■
Pot 5: 50% lunar simulant, 40% earth soil, 10% earthworm casings (no
compost or bone meal)
■
Pot 6: 100% lunar simulant
2.
Planting: Planted 3 radish seeds in each pot. Thinned to the healthiest sprout
post-germination.
3.
Measurements: Monitored weekly for:
○
Sprout count
○
Plant height
○
Leaf count
○
Radish formation
4.
Adjustments: Increased watering post-Thanksgiving break due to wilting.
Data Collection

Analysis
●
Best Growth: Pot 5 demonstrated the tallest height (6 cm), but Pot 4 had the highest
sprout count by Week 2. However, no radishes formed in any pot.
●
Amendments: Pots with compost and bone meal (Pots 2 and 4) showed healthier
leaves and better sprouting compared to those without.
●
Challenges: Watering inconsistencies during Thanksgiving break led to wilting,
impacting final growth outcomes.
Conclusions
Our hypothesis was partially supported. While Pot 5 achieved the best height, the lack of radish
formation suggests that even the best soil amendments were insufficient for radish development
in lunar simulant. Nutrient adding appears critical but needs further refinement.
Future Considerations
●
Test additional amendments to improve nutrient availability.
●
Experiment with more consistent watering schedules to prevent stress.
●
Explore different crops better suited to low-nutrient conditions.
Reflection
This experiment highlighted the complexities of growing crops in simulated lunar soil. The most
surprising discovery was the difference in sprouting between pots with and without
amendments. Our study contributes to understanding the challenges of lunar agriculture and the
importance of soil amendments for future missions.
